deXuat.trich: # Design Space Explore An engineering team designing a part rarely has one answer. They have a **design space** — a range of possible designs bounded by what they're allowed to vary (wall thickness, rib count, hole pattern, material) and what the part must satisfy (envelope, mass, load, cost, manufacturability). Modeling one design at a time, by hand, means evaluating three to five options and picking the best of a small set. This skill generates many at once, directly in the CAD tool the engineer already has open. **It does not design from scratch.** It takes a model the engineer already has and generates variants of it — that constraint is what makes the output trustworthy and reviewable rather than a pile of new geometry nobody asked for. **It does not run analysis.** It produces the variants and the manifest describing them, so an analysis tool or a person evaluates each one and retu

deXuat.mo: Produces the make-to-order quote from the intake form, comparable prior jobs and cost history, with every number traced to where it came from — material at the price actually paid
deXuat.trich: # Quote Build Pricing a make-to-order job means building up a cost and then applying commercial judgment. Every job is priced fresh, which is why quoting is skilled, slow, expert work — and why the estimator is usually the bottleneck. **The cost basis is shown, always.** A quote that says *$14,720* is useless. One that says *$14,720, of which $6,100 is material at the price we paid on PO-8841 in June, plus 8% scrap* is defensible. **Quick start** ``` → Load the intake form. Lines with no quantity or no material are skipped; quote the rest and list what's blocked → Find comparables; show what made each one comparable AND how this job differs → Flag capability BEFORE pricing. Then hours per op from the ladder: routing → actuals → confirmed design → first principles → Setup and run separate at every rung. A superseded routing is shown, never priced. probable_standard never outranks rung 3 →

deXuat.mo: Writing or reviewing a survey or questionnaire: customer feedback, NPS, CSAT, CES, pricing, market research, an in-app survey. Starts from the decision, asks about facts, pilots it
deXuat.trich: ## Survey Design **Send a survey only when you know which decision it informs.** Most bad surveys fail before the first question: no goal, the wrong people, questions nobody tested. Use this skill to take a survey from the decision to the analysis, or to review one. It draws on Caroline Jarrett's *Surveys That Work* and Annie Pettit's *People Aren't Robots*. ### Is it a survey at all? | You need | Use | |---|---| | Why people do something, in their own words | customer interviews, with a handful of people | | How common something is across a population | a survey: this skill | | What the people in a room think, right now | a live poll (below) | | Whether people can use something | a usability test | **When the people are in the room, poll them live instead of sending a form.** A workshop, a webinar, an all-hands or a customer advisory session answers in seconds, while everyone is there.
